texts.orig: What made Airbnb so special? ▶️
texts.text: What made Airbnb so special? ▶️

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Airbnb felt like a group of friends with a special bond working on a project rather than a job. Folks were diverse, including former founders and people outside the technology industry, which contributed to better decision-making and a YC-like mindset.
texts.text: Airbnb felt like a group of friends with a special bond working on a project rather than a job. Folks were diverse, including former founders and people outside the technology industry, which contributed to better decision-making and a YC-like mindset.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: The most important thing Airbnb looked for in early hires is how excited they were to be there. The second thing was to understand their true motivations and make sure they mapped to the company’s core values. Airbnb did this through “culture interviews.”

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Motivations can be diverse: solving technical problems, proving oneself, having a grand mission, or simply wanting to be successful. Motivation doesn’t necessarily determine success, and we have seen motivations change over time, e.g. just running the company and enjoying the process of building something big, even if the idea is not grand or shiny.
texts.text: Motivations can be diverse: solving technical problems, proving oneself, having a grand mission, or simply wanting to be successful. Motivation doesn’t necessarily determine success, and we have seen motivations change over time, e.g. just running the company and enjoying the process of building something big, even if the idea is not grand or shiny.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Being clear on the motivations also improves conflict resolution and self-awareness among co-founders.
texts.text: Being clear on the motivations also improves conflict resolution and self-awareness among co-founders.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Don’t start a company as a career step: If you’re successful, it will most likely be your entire career, and if it’s not successful, that’s not something you generally aspire to.
texts.text: Don’t start a company as a career step: If you’re successful, it will most likely be your entire career, and if it’s not successful, that’s not something you generally aspire to.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Consider personal constraints: Startups are hard, so don’t do it if you have financial, family, or relationship constraints that are more important.

texts.text: The magic that happens at YC Office Hours ▶️

texts.label: text
texts.orig: YC Office Hours come in two types: Regular Office Hours (one-on-one) and Group Office Hours (with multiple startups).
texts.text: YC Office Hours come in two types: Regular Office Hours (one-on-one) and Group Office Hours (with multiple startups).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Regular Office Hours key question: “What’s holding you back from moving faster?”
texts.text: Regular Office Hours key question: “What’s holding you back from moving faster?”

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Group Office Hours key question: “What are your goals for the next two weeks and what were your goals for the last two weeks? Did you hit the goals? If not, what came in the way of hitting the goals?”
texts.text: Group Office Hours key question: “What are your goals for the next two weeks and what were your goals for the last two weeks? Did you hit the goals? If not, what came in the way of hitting the goals?”

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Addresses the loneliness of the founders by allowing them to lean on others who share similar problems and anxieties.
texts.text: Addresses the loneliness of the founders by allowing them to lean on others who share similar problems and anxieties.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Creates accountability by having founders share their goals and progress every two weeks.
texts.text: Creates accountability by having founders share their goals and progress every two weeks.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Founders in coworking spaces should schedule time to talk, because by default they end up working by themselves with headphones on and no time for interaction. YC’s best experiences were in person, with everyone paying attention to each other without distractions.

texts.orig: Common reasons startups fail ▶️
texts.text: Common reasons startups fail ▶️

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Failing to find product-market fit because they don’t talk to customers:
texts.text: Failing to find product-market fit because they don’t talk to customers:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Often because they think software is the solution to everything, or because they’re afraid of rejection. Ninety percent of customers are not early adopters, so they’re not incentivized to take risks and try something new, and you need to reach out to 10 customers to be able to find that one.
texts.text: Often because they think software is the solution to everything, or because they’re afraid of rejection. Ninety percent of customers are not early adopters, so they’re not incentivized to take risks and try something new, and you need to reach out to 10 customers to be able to find that one.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: External validation (e.g. investments, praise) is often confused with product-market fit, leading to neglect of customer input. One of the most important moments in Airbnb history was Paul Graham asking the founders of Airbnb, “Where are your customers?,” to which they said, “Oh, they’re in New York,” and Graham responded, “So why are you talking to me and not in New York right now talking to them?”

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: Having an idea and trying to find technical co-founder to build it is like having an idea for a song and looking for a musician to make it. Engineering is really hard and valuable.
